title: sampled-batch consensus allocator and quant stitcher blueprint
author: Mira Patel
description:
Motivation: large tenants exhibit multi-modal request patterns that make single-strategy batching suboptimal. This PR introduces a sampled-batch consensus allocator that forms lightweight consensus decisions across concurrent samplers and attaches a tenant-aware quant stitcher that composes conservative quantization profiles at rollout time. The goal is to reduce per-token cost without regressing p95 latency or quality for high-variance workloads.

What this change contains: implementation of a sampled consensus layer in the runtime batcher so multiple samplers can propose batch groupings and a consensus step selects the batch plan with best predicted unit-econ score; a new quant stitcher service that merges safe quantization presets (CPU/GPU/INT8/FP16) based on historical eval signals and per-tenant safety thresholds; telemetry hooks (unit_econ.* and batch.consensus.* metrics) and a small CLI to generate dry-run profiles for tenant owners.

Design notes: consensus uses a probabilistic sampling window (configurable, default 150ms) across N samplers to estimate expected token/latency tradeoffs. Scoring function is pluggable and evaluates expected cost delta against a latency SLO penalty. Quant stitcher merges candidate quant profiles by ranking them on a loss-tolerant score computed from recent eval sets and sentinel prompts; the stitcher emits a safe combined profile and a degradation estimate. Rollout uses canary rules in the console (canary weight + rollback thresholds) tied to the new telemetry alarms.

Backward compatibility: runtime defaults unchanged. New behaviors gated by two flags: runtime.batcher.consensus.enabled (off by default) and quant.stitcher.automerge (off by default). This lets operators evaluate via dry-run.

Testing: unit tests for the consensus allocator, synthetic workloads in perf-canary, integration tests for stitcher + eval harness, and a smoke test that runs a tenant-level dry-run and verifies no p95 regression under 99% simulated traffic.

Migration and rollout: docs/blueprints/sample-consensus.md contains a step-by-step tenant migration guide. Recommend enabling consensus in staging with automerge=false for 2 weeks before gradual canary.

Related: ENG-1952 (tenant economizer RFC), ENG-1960 (quant safety signals), SUP-421 incident followup where bursty tenants saw cost spikes.

Checklist: - [x] Runtime consensus allocator implementation - [x] Quant stitcher service and API - [x] Telemetry and alert rules - [x] CLI dry-run + docs - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf canary run and baseline attached to the PR

Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative in default behavior to avoid surprise regressions. The quant stitcher emits both a recommended profile and a conservative fallback; the platform will only activate the recommended profile when tenant owners opt in or when policy allows automated rollouts with safe thresholds.
